items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1976-02-19
items.q: I mentioned that he was the nephew of Don Albert, who is a, or the uncle of Don Albert, who is a band leader, an old New Orleans band leader of a black, orchestra.

ctx.x: intellectual considerations. No, but you have to take, you have to start taking them in considerations when you see that the music is being, is being threatened of extinction, of

extinction. Well, the music is extinct. Well, okay. You see? And I think it's, I think, to, to, to, what do you do about that? I mean, what's your reaction to that? Let me ask you that. My reaction to it is, I suppose you could say a fatalistic one that I would have had to accept the fact that this could happen, you see, but what I resist is, is a concept like a very good friend of mine, very prominent in the jazz world. We were discussing some time ago, Natty Dominique, who is a Chicago, lives in Chicago, but is…
Even though jazz always has a racial tag attached to it, to many people.
